prose.summary: The product meets the rule of origin, so the CEPA rate – the reduced rate under the India-UAE CEPA – can be claimed. This reduces the normal (MFN) rate, which is the duty charged when no trade‑agreement preference is claimed, from 30% to 0%, saving an estimated 8100.00 USD.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 19053100, Sweet biscuits. Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but the code should be confirmed with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 30% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The estimated saving is 8100.00 USD.
prose.origin: The rule of origin requires a change in tariff heading (CTH) and at least 40% value addition (VA). CTH means each non‑originating input must be classified in a different four‑digit heading than the product, and VA is the share of the product’s price that does not come from non‑originating materials. The final manufacture check – whether the last manufacturing step took place in the UAE – is satisfied, and the minimal operations check – whether the work goes beyond simple operations that never give origin on their own – is also satisfied. The CTH requirement is met because all three non‑originating inputs are classified outside heading 1905, and the VA requirement is met with a build‑down of 55.0% on an FOB basis, where FOB is the price loaded on board at the UAE port, exceeding the 40% threshold.

notes.text: India's tariff schedule marks the 30% MFN rate with a footnote that Mansha has not checked; confirm the normal rate with Indian customs or a customs broker.
The '+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Operations and final manufacture are the exporter's own declaration.
The duty estimate is on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, the Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is likely charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text on it was found). Anti-dumping and safeguard duties likely still apply (no CEPA exemption from them was found).

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement. The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
